blocks.text: Chapter 12 presents Jerusalem and Judah together under attack from surrounding nations, while Jehovah’s protection overturns the assault and preserves Jerusalem. The chapter also resists a simple hierarchy within Judah: Judah is saved first so that the prominence of David’s house and Jerusalem’s inhabitants is not elevated above it. Its final movement shifts from deliverance to grief, joining an outpoured spirit, attention to a pierced figure, and intense mourning carried out separately by named families and their wives.
